reconciliation.note: Opened on the campaign itself rather than by drilling one of its search terms, so the Term columns have nothing to report and refuse rather than reading zero.

placements.note: Every target here sits in ONE campaign, and Amazon reports placement per campaign — so the share percentages are that campaign's own measured split and are IDENTICAL on every row. Compare targets on the COUNT columns, which really do differ, and read the shares across a row rather than down a column. What the counts are worth reading against is the effective bid for the same slot, three columns to the left: what we bid there, and what we got for it.

notInMatrix.realAcos: Real ACOS (waste-adjusted) has no field in the metric matrix at syntax grain yet.
notInMatrix.clickShare: SQP click share has no field in the metric matrix at syntax grain yet.
notInMatrix.placementUnits: Units at placement are an ESTIMATE built from two: the estimated clicks there (a dense fold) times the estimated units-per-click, which is an index on this row's own rate in the CVR's construction. A direct split is impossible — units appear in only 711 of 2,564 Top-of-Search campaign-placement cells, the SAME 711 that carry sales. On this account units and orders are near-identical (8,653 of 8,803 cells have them equal, 1.03 units per order), so this tracks clicks x the estimated CVR closely; it is here because units are the unit you act on.
notInMatrix.placementOffRate: Off Amazon is withheld from the estimated CTR, CVR and ACOS by the ruling of 2026-08-30: of 117 campaigns with an Off Amazon placement row, 101 had ZERO orders there, and it recorded sales in 52 of 603 placement cells. Rendered as a number it would read as a claim about how Off Amazon converts, which the data cannot support either way. Its impressions, clicks, spend and CPC are shown — those legs are well evidenced.

contract: campaign x target x day: what the campaign BIDS ON, which is not a partition of the search term above it — these rows carry the campaign's whole traffic on each target, while the campaign row carries one term's slice of the campaign. The Term columns are the bridge between the two.

rows.bidNote: A SNAPSHOT, not a window figure: the bid as of 2026-09-23, which is the latest the collector stamped onto this target inside the selected days. It does not move with the date range the way every measure beside it does, and a target whose bid changed mid-window shows only where it ended.
rows.effBidTosNote: $1.38 base x 3.25 (+225% at Top of Search on-Amazon), the modifier as of 2026-09-22. Under Dynamic — down only Amazon may bid less than this and never more, so it is a true ceiling.
rows.effBidRosNote: $1.38 base x 1.00 (+0% at Other on-Amazon (rest of search)), the modifier as of 2026-09-22. Under Dynamic — down only Amazon may bid less than this and never more, so it is a true ceiling.
rows.effBidPdpNote: $1.38 base x 1.00 (+0% at Detail Page on-Amazon), the modifier as of 2026-09-22. Under Dynamic — down only Amazon may bid less than this and never more, so it is a true ceiling.
rows.tosImpressionShareReason: Top-of-search impression share is published in the KEYWORD report only, and this target has no row there — auto and product targets never do.
rows.termSpendReason: No search term is in scope: this level was opened on the campaign itself, not by drilling one of its terms.

notes: Every rate is BLENDED — the window's total over its total (spend over sales, clicks over impressions) — never the mean of daily or per-row rates.

Sales, orders and every rate built on them carry 7-day attribution: the trailing seven days are still filling in and read LOW. The newest day is also a partial day. Compare settled windows with settled windows.
Targets are what we BID ON (keywords, ASINs, auto groups). Bids are read from the daily bid snapshots, not the report's own bid column, which is stamped at report time.
